scope_note: Light verification/polish pass. Joey coverage already spans Lantana/Verbena habit and floral architecture. This package verifies the modern family circumscription, repairs missing Aloysia/Lantana mappings, and adds the fruit/style characters needed to distinguish Verbenaceae from Lamiaceae.

joey_coverage.assessment: Joey coverage is sufficient for habit/leaf/flower recognition. The missing teaching piece was fruit plus the terminal-style/indeterminate-inflorescence distinction from Lamiaceae.

family_lesson.where_to_look_first: Start with opposite/decussate simple leaves without stipules, then look at the inflorescence: modern Verbenaceae is strongly associated with indeterminate racemose spikes or heads rather than the cymose/verticillaster architecture typical of many Lamiaceae. Confirm with a tubular flower, superior ovary, terminal style, and genus-specific dry or drupaceous fruit.
family_lesson.strongest_field_confirmation: Opposite exstipulate leaves + racemose/spicate/capitate inflorescence + tubular usually zygomorphic corolla + superior ovary with terminal style + fruit that is a dry/fleshy schizocarp or drupe/pyrene system.
authoritative_framework: Herbs, shrubs or small trees; branchlets may be terete or quadrangular.
Leaves usually opposite/decussate or whorled; stipules absent.
Inflorescences indeterminate and racemose, often spikes or compact heads.
Flowers usually 4- or 5-merous and zygomorphic to weakly bilabiate.
Ovary superior, syncarpous, often entire or only slightly/moderately 4-lobed.
Style terminal rather than characteristically gynobasic.
Fruit highly informative: dry/fleshy schizocarps, 2- or 4-part mericarps, or drupaceous fruits with pyrenes.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not use square stems as a family separator; both Verbenaceae and Lamiaceae may have quadrangular stems.
Do not use aromatic foliage as a family separator; both families can be aromatic.
Do not assume all Verbenaceae fruits are dry; Lantana is drupaceous.
Do not assume all fruits split into four units; Phyla commonly resolves to two pyrenes/mericarps.
Do not treat terminal style versus gynobasic style as an absolute across all Lamiaceae; use it as a strong local/common-pattern distinction.
Do not count introduced/cultivated comparison rows as project-native species.

Verbenaceae: Inflorescences usually indeterminate/racemose, often spikes or heads.
Ovary often entire or only shallowly/moderately lobed.
Fruit may be a dry schizocarp, fleshy schizocarp, or drupe with pyrenes.
Lamiaceae: Ovary commonly deeply 4-lobed in the classic local herbaceous pattern.
Style commonly gynobasic in that classic pattern.
Fruit commonly four nutlets, though drupaceous exceptions such as Callicarpa exist.
lamiaceae_comparison.field_rule: If the stem and opposite leaves say 'mint-like', stop using stem shape. Move to inflorescence architecture, ovary/style position and mature fruit.

fruit_lesson.key_point: Fruit is the best final separator because the local family spans several architectures.
sequence: Verbena/Glandularia: persistent calyx opened to show four dry one-seeded mericarps.
Phyla: tiny fruit split into two pyrenes/mericarps.
Lantana: fleshy purple-black drupe cut open to show hard endocarp/stone.
Place all three beside a classic Lamiaceae four-nutlet fruit.

taxonomy_and_native_status_notes: Aloysia gratissima is accepted by POWO and native Arizona to Texas southward.
Aloysia virgata is accepted but native South America; comparison only.
Glandularia bipinnatifida and G. pumila are accepted by POWO and native in Texas.
Lantana urticoides is accepted and native Texas.
Lantana camara is accepted but its native range is Mexico to Tropical America; project row is cultivated-only.
Lantana × strigocamara is an accepted hybrid and listed as introduced in Texas.
Verbena halei is accepted and native in Texas.
Verbena brasiliensis is accepted but introduced in Texas.
fast_key: Opposite exstipulate leaves + racemose spike/head + terminal style -> strongly supports Verbenaceae.
Long slender simple/panicled spikes + dry four-mericarpy fruit -> Verbena.
Contracted flower head + dry four-mericarpy fruit -> Glandularia.
Creeping mat rooting at nodes + tiny compact heads + two-pyrene fruit -> Phyla.
Woody rough-leaved colorful head + fleshy dark drupe -> Lantana.
Woody aromatic shrub + narrow axillary white racemes -> Aloysia.
Opposite leaves + interpetiolar stipules + inferior ovary -> Rubiaceae, not Verbenaceae.
Deeply 4-lobed ovary + gynobasic style + cymose/verticillaster inflorescence -> classic Lamiaceae pattern.
